plan: Initialize CheckInConsole with a copied appointment list, optional injected action_source/screen_sink ports, and a public session dict holding exactly active/contact_confirmed/appointment_id/completed in their initial values.

Centralize screen construction in one builder that emits {prompt, messages, choices}, attaching freshly built appointment choices in input order exactly when the prompt is 'Choose appointment'; a companion error builder emits an 'Error:'-prefixed first message with empty choices.

Dispatch handle(action) through a per-type handler table; each handler validates preconditions and payload types fully before mutating session, so invalid or malformed actions (including non-dicts and unknown types) return an error screen with accepted data untouched and never raise.

Implement prompt progression per contract: begin -> 'Confirm contact'; confirm_contact -> 'Choose appointment' iff confirmed else 'Confirm contact'; correct -> next unmet prompt; choose -> 'Review and complete'; complete -> 'Check-in complete' with ['Checked in'] and marks completed/inactive; abandon -> 'Session abandoned' with ['Check-in abandoned'] and resets session.

run_once raises RuntimeError before touching either port when one is missing, otherwise performs exactly one read_action(), one handle(), one display(screen), and returns the same screen object, so both ports are replaceable by plain stdlib unittest fakes.
mechanisms: single authoritative session dictionary mutated only after full validation
dedicated screen-builder deriving deterministic screen dicts from state
handler-table action interpreter with validate-before-mutate discipline
error-screen path that explains rejection without state change or exceptions
constructor-injected action_source/screen_sink ports for test replacement
